reasons: Classification is correct: the only vendor-side warranty is a narrow Y2K date-processing warranty, so there is no professional/workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy — the clause fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) rather than merely falling short of preferred.

Redline is actionable and well-placed: the new warranty and remedy language is inserted at the end of Section 9 (TrueLink Warranties), leaving existing text intact, and tracks the model language (professional and workmanlike services, conformance for a stated period, compliance with laws, no malicious code, vendor-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund).

Comment is accurate (correctly notes the Section 12 disclaimer carve-out has nothing to carve out), concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, and expressly offers the 90/30-day fallback.

Minor and acceptable: the inserted conformance warranty adds 'specifications agreed by the parties' and no separate services-warranty duration, small expansions beyond the model wording that do not change the substance or make the edit disproportionate; deterministic checks pass.
